acquisition_method.evidence: DDA LC-MS/MS Analysis of Single Samples and Fractionated Peptides for the Label-Free Approach
The mass spectrometry method utilized MS1 scans alternated with looped 18 narrow window DIA scans covering m/z range from 450 to 1,080.

alkylation_concentration.evidence: The proteins were reduced with 4.5 mM DTT at 60 °C for 20 minutes followed by alkylation with 11 mM iodoacetamide at room temperature for 15 minutes in the dark.

alkylation_reagent.evidence: The proteins were reduced with 4.5 mM DTT at 60 °C for 20 minutes followed by alkylation with 11 mM iodoacetamide at room temperature for 15 minutes in the dark.

cleavage_agent.evidence: The sample was then diluted 4-fold to a final concentration of 2 M urea, 20 mM HEPES, pH 8.0, and trypsin digestion was carried out overnight at 37 °C with an enzyme/substrate ratio of 1/50.

collision_energy.evidence: Sixteen tandem mass spectra were collected in a data-dependent manner following each survey scan using 60 second exclusion for previously sampled peptide peaks and normalized collision energy set to 28.

The same UPLC and mass spectrometry instrument parameters were used as described above except in MS2 where the first mass was set to m/z 100 to include the reporter ions and the normalized collision energy value was set to 30.

fractionation_method.evidence: For LF, an aliquot (600 µg) of total protein digest was fractionated using basic pH reversed phase HPLC, adapted from the method published by Mertins et al.
bRPLC separation was carried out on Dionex Ultimate3000 UPLC using a 2.1 mm ID×50 mm column (XBridge, Waters) packed with C18, 3.5 µM particle size at a 0.2 ml/min flow rate.

instrument.evidence: A nanoflow ultra high performance liquid chromatograph (RSLC, Dionex, Sunnyvale, CA) interfaced with an electrospray quadrupole-orbital ion trap mass spectrometer (QExactive Plus, Thermo, San Jose, CA) was used for tandem mass spectrometry peptide sequencing experiments.
